description: Global cross-stock news dedup emptied the feed. is_duplicate_news() compared each incoming title against every title from the last 7 days ACROSS ALL STOCKS at 75% similarity, so one ticker's market-wide headline ('Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Rises') permanently blocked every other ticker's near-identical one. The whole DB held 332 articles.
resolution: Scope dedup to ONE stock within a +/-72h window (services/dedup.py). Identity is a canonical URL hash enforced by UNIQUE(short_name, url_hash); near-duplicates cluster by normalised title key or token_set_ratio>=88 and elect the best copy by source rank, then image, then description. DB went 332 -> 3,212 articles. Regression test: tests/test_db.py::test_the_same_headline_is_stored_for_two_different_stocks.

description: Yahoo's per-ticker endpoints (v1/finance/search news, feeds.finance.yahoo.com RSS) look symbol-keyed but silently fall back to GENERIC MARKET NEWS for thin tickers. Querying IVU.DE returned a Fed rates story, a Hormuz shipping story and a Jersey Mike's IPO notice, all tagged as relevant to IVU.
resolution: Only Finviz's quote-page table (genuinely hand-curated) may contribute articles that do not name the stock; those are tagged relevance='related'. Yahoo and Google results must name the stock, ticker or resolved alias or they are dropped. After the change IVU returned 9 articles, all actually about IVU Traffic Technologies AG. See dedup._RELATED_ALLOWED.

description: Advertising 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br' without a brotli decoder installed makes httpx return raw brotli bytes. Status is 200, length is plausible (44KB), BeautifulSoup parses it into a document with no tables, and the scraper reports 'no news' with no error at all. Finviz serves brotli.
resolution: brotli is a HARD dependency in pyproject.toml, not an extra, because the header promises it. The same trap awaits zstd if copied from a current Chrome header set. When a parser can legitimately return nothing, assert the input looked like the expected format so 'quiet source' and 'broken source' are distinguishable.

title: Keep Google News redirect links instead of resolving publisher URLs
rationale: The token redirects correctly in a browser, so the link works as-is. Attribution comes from the feed's <source> element mapped through services/news/publishers.py, costing zero extra requests. Side benefit: those articles rank lower in dedup tie-breaks, so a Finviz copy carrying a real reuters.com URL wins the cluster, which is the outcome we want anyway.

title: Price sources: Yahoo chart v8 primary, CNBC fallback; Stooq and Google Finance rejected
rationale: Stooq rejected: now behind a JS bot-wall and its quote endpoint 404s. Google Finance rejected: markup JS-obfuscated, no price in the HTML. Yahoo v7 bulk quote rejected: needs a cookie+crumb dance and is unnecessary at watchlist scale, where per-symbol chart calls also return history. History is Yahoo-only, so a Yahoo outage degrades to quote-only rather than breaking.

content: All outbound HTTP goes through services/http_client.py (the shared 'scraper' instance). Never add a bare requests/httpx call in a scraper module.
